match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the cultural and spiritual meaning of landforms for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples: the first two cover basic landform and landscape types, and the Uluru card is a Year 9 point about park management and tourism, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Landscapes in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures
card: For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, Country is more than land. It includes the land, waters, sky, plants and animals, and the stories and laws that go with them.

Many landforms hold deep cultural and spiritual meaning. They are part of Dreaming stories, which are passed down through generations and explain how the land came to be and how people should care for it.
Uluru in the Northern Territory is a sacred place for the Anangu people. Its story, law and ceremony are connected to the rock and its surrounds.
Gariwerd, also called the Grampians, in Victoria is important to the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples. It holds sacred sites, stories and rock art.
draft.remember: For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, landforms are part of Country, with stories, law and spiritual meaning.

a.q: Why is Uluru so important to the Anangu people?
opts: It is a sacred place linked to their stories and law
It is the only landform in the Northern Territory
It is valued only for how it looks to visitors
It is a place where the Anangu no longer live
a.why: For the Anangu, Uluru is part of Country, with stories, law and ceremony tied to it. It is not only a tourist sight, because its meaning is cultural and spiritual as well as visual.
a.clue: Think about what Country means to the Anangu.

b.q: A Year 7 class in Victoria visits the Grampians. Which statement best describes how Gariwerd is seen by the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples?
opts: As Country with sacred sites, stories and rock art
As a mountain range valued only for its height
As a place with no connection to Dreaming stories
As land that belongs to the Anangu people
b.why: Gariwerd is Country for the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples, and it holds sacred sites, stories and rock art. Seeing it only as a mountain range misses its cultural and spiritual meaning.
b.clue: Gariwerd is the name used by the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples.

a.best: It is a sacred place linked to their stories and law

b.best: As Country with sacred sites, stories and rock art

problems.detail: The wrong options are implausible ('the only landform in the Northern Territory', 'a place where the Anangu no longer live'). Students can pick the answer by elimination without knowing the idea.
The wrong options are easy to rule out ('no connection to Dreaming stories', 'belongs to the Anangu', 'valued only for its height'). The question barely tests understanding.

check.summary: The facts are correct, the intended answers are right and the explanations agree with the card. The only issue is that both questions have weak, implausible distractors, so they are very easy to answer by elimination.

proposal.title: Landscapes in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures
card: For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, Country includes the land, waters, sky, plants and animals, and the stories and law tied to them. People belong to Country and care for it.
Many landforms are part of Dreaming stories, which explain how the land formed and how to care for it. These stories are passed down through generations and are still part of life and law today.
Uluru in the Northern Territory is sacred to the Anangu people. Their law and stories, called Tjukurpa, are tied to the rock and the land around it.
Gariwerd, also called the Grampians, in Victoria is Country for the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples. It holds sacred sites, stories and rock art.
proposal.remember: Landforms are part of Country, with stories, law and spiritual meaning that continue today.

a.q: What does Country mean for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples?
opts: Land, waters, sky and living things, with stories and law
The land a group owns, set by legal boundaries on a map
The rural parts of Australia, away from towns and cities
Landforms such as hills and rocks, but not waters or sky
a.why: Country takes in the land, waters, sky, plants and animals, and the stories and law tied to them. It is not the rural 'country' or a legal title. Limiting it to landforms on land misses the waters, sky and stories it also includes.
a.clue: Country covers more than what you can stand on.

b.q: A ranger at Gariwerd tells a Year 8 class that some rock art sites are protected and closed to visitors. Which reason best explains why they matter to the Aboriginal peoples of Gariwerd?
opts: They are sacred sites, still tied to stories and law today
They are relics of a culture that has now disappeared
They are mainly scenic spots kept safe for tourists
They are sacred to the Anangu, whose Country it is
b.why: Gariwerd is Country for the Djab Wurrung and Jardwadjali peoples, and its sacred sites are tied to stories and law that are still part of life today. The Anangu option is tempting because it says sacred, but the Anangu are the people of Uluru, not Gariwerd.
b.clue: Check which peoples Gariwerd belongs to, and whether the connection has ended.
